chunks: And also, ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: Inform me about one who is absent from his wife and commits zina—would he be stoned if he has a wife while he is away from her? He said, “The one absent from his wife is not stoned, nor the one who has contracted marriage but has not consummated with his wife, nor the one who has a mutʿah wife.” I said: Then at what limit of his journey is he not considered muḥṣan? He said, “When he shortens the prayer and breaks the fast, then he is not muḥṣan.”

key_terms.أَفْطَرَ: broke the sawm due to travel
key_terms.الْغَائِبِ: one who is absent, specifically away from his wife
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally in a state of iḥṣān for the zina ruling

ai.seo_question: When is a married man not considered muḥṣan for the hadd of zina in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the conditions of iḥṣān in the law of zina. It states that a man who is away from his wife, one who has not consummated marriage, and one in mutʿah are not treated as muḥṣan for the ruling of rajm; the travel threshold is identified as the point at which salat is shortened and sawm is broken.
